title: Proof flawed
statement: Prove that for every integer $n$ the number $n^5 + 5n^3 - 6n$ is divisible by $6$.
hints: Look at the factors of the expression.
Factorise it: a product of three consecutive integers appears, which settles divisibility by $2$ and by $3$.
solution: Checking $n = 1$ gives $0$ and $n = 2$ gives $60$, and both are divisible by $6$. So the claim holds for every integer $n$. Why this works. polynomial-factoring: the factorisation shows three consecutive integers.

rubric.criterion: Factorises the expression or reduces to residues.
